_invariant: b00t-mcp MUST carry args ['--stdio']. With args [] it takes the HTTP path: syncs the official MCP registry over the network, spawns npx bridges for every stdio entry (recursively bridging pi itself), prints usage, and exits — so the MCP handshake never happens. PiAdapter::enforce_stdio() repairs violations on every install.

b00t-mcp._toolPrefix: b00t-mcp already namespaces its own tools (b00t_*, soul_*). A server prefix would yield b00t_b00t_exec, so keep names clean.
b00t-mcp._directTools: Promote the discover->exec core to first-class pi tools. The niche soul_*/pipeline tools stay behind the ~200-token `mcp` proxy tool.

codebase-memory._args: Unlike b00t-mcp, codebase-memory-mcp defaults to stdio with no args — args [] is correct here.
codebase-memory._directTools: 'search' registers all 14 tools as real pi tools with real schemas but INACTIVE; mcp({search}) activates matches additively. Zero standing context cost, and they do not count toward the adapter's 75-tool advisory.
codebase-memory._why: codebase-memory-mcp auto-detects Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Zed, OpenCode, Aider, KiroCode — but NOT pi, so its own `install` subcommand will never wire pi. PiAdapter is what registers it here.
